newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile's Frei to keep pushing for 'normal democracy'.
newsitem.headline: Chile's Frei to keep pushing for 'normal democracy'.

text.p: President Eduardo Frei vowed on Wednesday to keep pushing for reforms to Chile's constitution to reduce the military's political power and create a "democracy with no strings attached," despite defeat in Congress for his proposals.

Frei pressed legislators to eliminate nine military-appointed Senate seats and other privileges for the armed forces, accusing the rightists who have resisted the reforms of "impeding our progress toward a new era."

"We want for Chile a normal democracy with no strings attached. Nothing more and nothing less," said Frei in his annual speech to Congress which meets in the port of Valparaiso. "We will not rest until our democracy is free of the authoritarian enclaves that limit the people's representation and sovereignty."
Chile returned to civilian rule in 1990 when dictator Gen. Augusto Pinochet handed over power after losing a plebiscite on his rule.

But under a 1981 constitution dictated by Pinochet, four Senate seats are reserved for retired military commanders and the military has an influential role in the appointment of five others. One of the nine seats is currently vacant.

The military also dominates two powerful state councils. Despite his title as commander-in-chief of the armed forces, Frei is constitutionally barred from firing or sending into retirement any officer without permission from a commander -- in the case of the army, Pinochet, who is army chief.
The 81-year-old Pinochet is also entitled to a lifetime Senate seat under his own constitution.
Frei's efforts to abolish most of those privileges were defeated in Congress last year, with the votes of the military appointees. Another effort this year looks headed for defeat.
Opponents of the reforms were "trying to erect a sort of barrier, out of stubbornness, to a change that one way or another will have to come," said Frei.

In a major political reform, Frei also said he will propose a bill to allow Chileans to elect directly the country's 12 regional councils. The councils are currently appointed by elected municipal councils.

"This reform ... will strengthen the regional councils' legitimacy and indentification with the citizenry," said Frei in his three-hour speech, adding that he plans to propose a series of other electoral reforms to give voters more options.
